key_insight: RLVR can drive unbounded chain-of-thought language drift, especially on novel reasoning tasks, while supervised fine-tuning does not.
engineering_relevance: For frontier reasoning systems, improving CoT monitorability during RLVR may require a tradeoff with reward, performance, or both.
method: Theoretically prove RLVR optimization pressure permits unbounded language drift.
Show supervised fine-tuning does not produce the same drift behavior.
Empirically test drift on novel reasoning tasks where the desired behavior is not already present in the base model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports both formal proofs and empirical results indicating drift emerges during RLVR when the target behavior cannot be elicited from the base model.
watch_item: Attempts to constrain language drift may also constrain expected reward, limiting practical ways to improve interpretability without reducing performance.
paper_title: On Language Drift during RLVR Post-Training
